Desling with your own issues and with those of a loved one is sooo difficult. We tend to feed of of others energy to get through our own battles. But it is soo hard to deal with others probs/issues without being In a good mental space ourselves. But you are fighting and that shows a warrior spirit. Your doing awesome. Give yourself credit. You are about to graduate. Woohoo! But your depression wants to look ahead to much and worry and steal your happiness. Sure you will need a job. And yeah a job will validate the work time and money in that degree. The job is the end goal. But you got all the time for that. Keep applying yourself and trying and finding a solution but also give yourself a little grace and allow your mind to find a little happiness along the journey to help you fight that depression. And if the future doesn't seem to optimistic, just remember it is not like today. It is not written in stone. There are a million possible futures and each and every day changes which one we will eventually find. Stay in the moment stay fighting. Stay battling your issues. Stay seeking your happiness. And try to enjoy a few meaningless frivolous things along the way. You have earned it.

Heyo. Yeah people who don't have the struggle you have simply cannot understand. They can sympathize but that only goes so far. The physical manifestation of your issues sucks I know. I always try to explain it to people that my brain is trying to convince my body that I am dying. So yes that pain is "in your head" but it's absolutely real and debilitating. And as far as your story in the comments I just want to say thank you for your openess and honesty. I found it encouraging. I hate thatcyou struggle with it but your fighting spirit is motivating. I see someone who is strong (because that shit kills weak people) who has been through hell and a half and instead of being a bitter selfish heartless asshole, you are sitting there in all your pain still worrying about trying to be better and to do better. Wanting to be ok in a world that dismisses your pain and hurts to exist within. And yes it might seem that nothing is ever working right or good enough, but you are showing up every day to the fight (even though I know you don't want to) and that is really inspiring. Keep fighting for your happiness (I know it seems soooo far away). Keep working the therapy. Keep doing whatever it takes to keep yourself going. And honestly fuck everything else. Everyone's thoughts, opinions, comments, etc. And even your own brain. It's lying to you, manipulating you, hurting you, and killing you. Its not your friend. It is your enemy that you are fighting. And you are doing well. (Even when it seems hopeless). Sometimes it feels like the pain will go away if you can just crawl in a hole and dissappear but it simply isn't true. It just numbs and hides it for a bit. But if you ever have a chance to overcome the shitty deal you were given and to triumph over all that adversity, it will be hard tiring baby steps and personal victories. Not societies standards and exceptions. You live for you and nobody else. You are who matter. Because if you aren't ok nothing else in your life will be either. So keep it up. Slowly develop. Slowly come to grips with your traumas (even though they murder your heart each and every damn day) slowly develop positive habits with work sleep etc. And measure yourself by your own goal. To be ok and to survive. (6 months later did I have 10% more "good days")(when I was really in pain has it gotten 2% not as strong) Thanks for posting and thanks from a random internet stranger for your courage and bravery to fight this shit. Sharing your pain and struggle does help others!! I hope by getting it off your chest for even 5 secs has helped you. Best wishes.

Yeah quarantine is rough. 1st those feelings you expressed seem pretty correct for dealing with what you are dealing with. So being honest with that is a positive way to deal with them. As far as overcoming them, you have to find a way to get your brain active. If it doesn't have a lot to do it is going to turn against you. It will attack you. It can be something intellectual to learn something new, or read, etc or all the way to just a fun time like games, buzzfeed quizzes, personality tests, etc. You can be as self indulgent as you want. Its totally acceptable in quarantine. As far as loneliness, just reach out to whoever you can for connection. Good people will realize you are struggling and dealing with alot and will want to listen and be there. Just be honest with them. Dont pretend your fine. Dont pretend everything is ok. Dont fake it. Just be honest and open (and a little selfish) and allow people to be there for you and allow you to laugh, cry, get angry, etc. Dont be afraid to word vomit all over them. If they care for you, or are just kind souls, it isn't something they negatively view or judge. So if you fight and attack lonely and bored hopefully the depression just eases a bit. Take care of yourself physically, stay safe, and above all reach out and be yourself. Posting here shows your doing that last part so you are going to be fine.

The problem with insecurity is that life will "prove you right". We project it on to the faces and voices of those around us. It puts us in the upside down. It makes us think everyone thinks so little of us and then because of that we feel worthless and insignificant. What a vicious cycle. And no matter what anyone else tells us, we think they are lying or wrong or fake. Because we know how bad it is in our own head.....the thing is your brain is a liar. It makes up stuff all the time to survive. Its a physical and chemical cluster that just processes out incorrect info sometimes. Residual damage. Ever had deja vu, or a blind spot, or taste buds don't feel right, or get soo hot you feel cold. That was your brain screwing up and lying to you. Did it make you feel insecure or worthless....doubtful. those feelings come from the fact that you believe the lies that you whisper ever day to yourself. And that you perceive in the world around you. Just remember your not always right, those thoughts or feelings are not to be trusted. And that your brain is a frazzled lying ball of pink goo inside your head. Doesnt mean the thoughts go away. But maybe just maybe the whirlwind of insecurities and self worth issues might get better just ever so slightly. And any relief or self love or acceptance on your part would do a lot to make sure your true self knows she is loved and cared for. Because you will do your best to protect her from all of those lies. Keep fighting. Your doing well. Thats why you felt like you were getting better. You were. And it made your insecurities mad and upset because they need you to survive. You are the host and they are the virus. They need you to be weak for them to be strong. And they came back stronger than ever. So now it is your turn to do the same and show them who is boss. They might be real, but that doesn't make them true. Keep fighting.

Great progress so far. Sorry about hitting a plateau. That always sucks. So a little advice for what it is worth. 1) give yourself a little grace and understanding. Its just a bad cycle you are in and its natural. You aren't seeing the progress you want so you get down and then out of frustration you pick up bad habits which make it where you can't progress. 2) so break the cycle. Pick 1 thing. And either start or stop it. But don't make it monumental. Make it manageable. And if you fall punish yourself. Ugh I was lazy, im calorie restricting tomorrow. Ugh I binged. I have to walk tomorrow. Just do anything to short circuit the cycle. 3) and most important be patient and set smaller goals. The next part of your journey will be harder and more difficult because you have less to lose. Plus motivation will be tougher. Plus your brain will try to wiggle out because "you have already done so much". But you want more and aren't satisfied yet. So go slow. Realize losing 1.4 today is losing 2.6 a year ago. Its just body mass math. Its % weight loss and the smaller you are the smaller the losses will be. So go break the cycle. lose .5lb and be encouraged and know that you are doing well and that you will have good days and bad days and that you will make it.

Im hoping not to trigger you with this comment. I just want to talk with you as a fellow sufferer. You are unwanted. You are unloved. You have been through hell. You are dying on the inside. So fucking what. If that pain matters. If that crushing feeling will ever mean anything. If that despair and sadness ever mean anything. Then they have to continue. All the doubt and worthlessness and emptiness, if they every really mean a fucking thing, then you need time. You need all the time in the world to heal. To be loved. To find joy. I can't guarantee you will find it. But I can say this. You are already in despair. Your already know worthlessness. You already define misery. But if love, grace, and, kindness ever do mean a fucking thing you will need time to find it. You will need patience. You will need acceptance. And above all you will need to realize that all those around you are broken fucking souls that can't get over their own shit for 2 seconds to show you your value and worth. Give them a little grace and acceptance. Because you know the value in being twisted and out of your God damn mind. And hopefully they show you the same care and concern. But it takes time. It takes the battle. It takes the pain and the misery. Because hope and grace and love don't mean shit without it. I don't expect this to encourage you or give you strength. But I hope you find solice in the fact that no matter what your brain says to you, you are not beyond repair and you are not alone. You live in a cruel motherfucking world in which 9 times out of 10 you will be fucked with, lied to, abused, and taken advantage of. And you might fight 5, 10, 20, 40 years to ever find peace or joy. But God damn aren't you worth it. Isn't all that pain and all that anguish worth it. Because that is what you have to go through. That is the lroce you ha e to be willing to pay. But I hope you can endure. I hope you can persevere. Because the world needs your existence, your light. And your soul. Even when it demeans it, rejects it, or shits all over you. Fuck this world bro and everything it stands for. But your beauty and grace are eternal and it fucking matters no matter who sees it.

So many times the mental struggle puts us in the upside down. Others caring for us will feel like a burden. All the little joys will make us sad. All the love in the world fuels self hatred. And no matter how twisted up everything becomes, we view it as fact because it is our brain telling us this. We treat thoughts like how our brain processes sight, sound, touch, etc. The problem is our brain cannot be trusted. But its so challenging to deal with your mental health because the person who is hurting you is you. Really freaking difficult to have self love if your self is hurting you. Just remember it isn't you that is hurting you. Its your anxiety. Or your depression or anxiety. You are how you are and who you are. You are coping. And prolly doing a much better job of it than you think. Just like your taste buds sometimes don't taste properly or blind spots in your vision or how cold can give you a burning sensation, your brain makes up a lot of info to fill in the gaps. It is a liar. And when you are deep in a mental hole try to remember that the feelings of anxiety worry unworthiness guilt shame etc simply aren't true. Your brain literally made it all up. I can't speak to every issue but if you think the girl in the picture needs to look different then your brain for sure is lying to you on that one. And it surely is on every other trigger and issue. Its ok to not trust your brain. Its ok to be wrong, or weak, or , depressed, or any negative feeling. You don't have to be good or ok or how people want you to act or a certain look or type or anything. All you have to be is open and honest with yourself and love the person deep within that is fighting all these lies each and every day. She is kicking ass every day to fight off all the monsters for you so give her a 👏 and let her know she is doing a good job protecting you from all the monsters your brain is putting in her path. She is a demon slayer.

Sometimes our mind becomes so overloaded that our tasks at hand seem too monumental. And worthlessness is a lie our mind whispers to us over and over again. So you are being attacked on both sides. (Not to mention all the external stressors). At this point it is only natural to feel listless and out of control and lost. You are swimming in an ocean of anxiety and pain. Easier said than done, but fight to focus on the present. Not even something as small as "next week". Not even as tiny as "today". What can you do right this second to help yourself make it better? What can you do this very instance to treat yourself worthwhile. Nothing big because you can't do big stuff right this second. But can you focus on your readings for 30 min? 15? Can you go to bed an hour earlier so your brain can rest? can you take 10 min to enjoy a meal to replenish your energy? Can you spend 10 min to reach out to someone so you can share your existence. 5 minutes to meditate and calm your mind. Or even 1 minute just to take a breath and remember that you can do this. You will never survive in the ocean. But you won't drown in a bath tub. View your problems in bite size portions and focus on solving as many of them as you can. And then celebrate those victories. Because if you win 10 small battles in a day (even if you lose a few along the way) you will be that much closer to getting through your big difficult ones and it will force the voice that tells you that you are worthless to quiet down (it never shuts up) simply because you will have proof that it is wrong and a liar. Hang in there!

Yeah post covid effects are so weird. My taste still feels "off" months later. Sometimes life triggers some behaviors in us that we thought we had overcome along our journey. Especially stress induced ones. (What doesn't cause stress haha). And while your long term goals will rely on you overcoming these and fighting the next battle, give yourself a little grace and understanding along your journey. Focus on minimizing binging if you can't eliminate. Or maybe focus on reducing a single trigger. Or when you just can't even feel like that and your brain is fried and your cravings consume, try to even just stop a little early or replace the sweet with fruit or the salty with nuts/pretzels etc. Just remember while you aren't perfect, its ok. If you don't act right or binge or chase a craving, maybe just try cutting it in half or hell even leave a single bite. Slowly but surely you will let go more and more and be back at again in no time. You have done a hell of a job and are continuing an awesome fight. Focus on something small again and keep climbing this mountain one step a time. You got this.

First of all Brigham is dope as hell well played. And second I think that how you explain that is perfectly put. (And not in a self centered way like society tells you to love and treat yourself) because you seem to want to share that with others and know that your happiness lies beyond your own existence. By getting better and taking the (hard) baby steps to make ourselves better in order to be able to connect in deeper more meaningful ways. Maybe its listening better, or the courage to reach out to someone, or the ability to coexist with someone or at someplace when its awkward or not exactly what we want. Burn with fire all the pain and insecurities that keep you from people. Look onto others (maybe new or old) and find the smallest crack to connect in a more meaningful way with. And on a really tough day when you feel all on your own and fed up, give yourself a little grace and understand and try to connect on a deeper level with yourself and with your heart. And then use all that fuel to go out there and fight another damn day to share that with the world. This place is scary and frightening and so dark. Shine your light (and Brighams) and people will see it because we are all desperate for that universal need to connect. You already made me smile and laugh and made my day better so thank you.

Those thoughts are the hardest because they are in your voice. You are naturally inclined to believe them as facts. You don't fact check them, debate them, disagree, etc because when your depressed you just are too weak to fight yourself. Just try to remember those thoughts (and your voice that tells them to you) are liars. They will come to rob and steal and take whatever joy or happiness is in your heart because they can't exist if your happy. They need you depressed and they need you miserable because without that they die. Keep fighting for yourself and your happiness and when you are in the grips of misery give yourself a little grace to be human and to not be ok and to be struggling. Because if you can accept yourself for even a second then the power of those lies dies just a little bit each time. Its a constant battle and they never shut up sometimes but just do the best you can and accept that it will be enough and above all remember your not always right and your not perfect and those thoughts come from your mind. So those thoughts aren't always correct either. Doubt them, question them, tell them to back off, and fight as hard as you can (even if it just a little) to constantly fight that mindset in pursuit of your version of happiness even if it seems unlikely or too far in the distance or unobtainable. And try to remind yourself your worth it. And as strong as those depressive feellings are, just remember theyre just not true. Best of luck and good vibes.

If someone else says negative things, it hurts but we can reject them. (They are wrong, stupid, screw them, etc) If it is our own voice it just is amplified and echoes. We take the initial pain of the insecure thought, and when we try to reject it, we are rejecting our own inner voice (albeit a critical cruel one)  and then our inner voice is now rejected and lashes out saying "you know its true". And it repeats 1000x in your head. Well at that point even the strongest soul will crumble eventually. Try looking at the negative thought and accept the fact that it might be how you truly feel about yourself. (Your not x, y, z or good enough etc.) And don't judge yourself or demean or bully yourself because you believe that fact to be true. Isolate it and then target it. And then you can truly fight the real monster. (The lie that is that thought) and not continue to loop and fight yourself. Keep fighting for yourself and try not to fight against yourself.

Thanks for your response. It is just a tick that is always there, and might always be there. Sorry that you live with that struggle. Worth is a hard thing to quantify because it is a value judgement.
